key_insight: RM-VLM turns natural-language tasks into reward machines and uses visual grounding to guide reinforcement learning on tasks that depend on action history.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on manually engineered proposition labelling for image-based environments, potentially simplifying reward design for autonomous agents.
method: An LLM generates a reward machine encoding temporal task structure from a natural-language description.
A VLM grounds the machine’s propositions in image observations during policy learning.
A VLM-based value estimator assesses progress toward transitions to provide dense rewards.
evidence_signal: Across non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection, RM-VLM achieved higher task success rates than existing VLM-based reward methods; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Incorrect LLM-generated task logic or unreliable visual grounding could produce misleading rewards and require validation before deployment.
paper_title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
